subject: cul-tf-s
title: CUL.TF.S.------C.CONT.
description: Diagram in WAC-21, on the page where Braxton describes how Debussy in Europe and Harrison in America actualized cross-sectional extension by adopting non-western aesthetic material into western methodological form, and where he argues 'the future of a given extension is directly related to whether or not that extension can absorb the multi-informational and vibrational demands that relate to composite continuance.' (C)CUL-TF-S (cultural transfer shifts) is crossed with C-CONT (composite continuance): the question is what cultural transfer shifts have to do with composite continuance — i.e., whether borrowed cross-cultural material can hold the line of a tradition rather than fragmenting it. CUL-TF-S outputs to TRS (transition) and C-CONT (the crossing). C-CONT then feeds INFO-CON (information convergence) → PART (participation). A separate chain runs (R)ATTN (the reality of attraction) ← RE-ST (restructuralism), with ATTN branching to AFL-DY (affinity dynamics) and PROJ-DY (projectional dynamics) → T-C-IMP (time continuum implications). Structural argument: cultural transfer shifts produce composite continuance only via information convergence into participation — meaning Debussy/Harrison-style borrowings only count as composite-continuance if they make their way into actual participatory structures. The restructuralism→attraction sub-chain runs in parallel, producing affinity-dynamics and projectional-dynamics → time-continuum implications, but these are not on the cultural-transfer-shift main line. The diagram thus stages exactly the danger Braxton names: cross-sectional extension can register as restructuralism (interesting) without actually feeding composite continuance (necessary).
